newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tonen says cost cuts helped profits rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tonen says cost cuts helped profits rise in 1996.

text.p: Tonen Corp said on Tuesday that its efforts to reduce costs -- including cutting staff -- boosted its profits in the 1996 business year.
"Cost-cutting efforts proved to have a bigger impact than we imagined," managing director Takuya Fujimura told reporters.
The company earlier reported a parent current profit of 17.02 billion yen for the year to December 31, 1996, up 29.5 percent from 13.15 billion yen in 1995.
Fujimura said he believed scaling down the company"s staff had helped boost performance.
He said the number of staff had fallen to 2,130 from about 2,200 during the past year.

Tonen said sales of gasoline and kerosene rose in 1996, while sales of naphtha and crude oil declined. The drop in sales of naphtha was due to a routine shutdown for checks at one of its facilities, which caused operation rates to fall.
It said its total sales for 1996 rose to roughly 520.8 billion yen, up 18.8 percent from 1995.
The refiner, in which U.S. oil giants Exxon Corp and Mobil Corp each have a 25 percent stake, forecast a parent current profit of 17.00 billion yen for the current year.
